description: Table 3 is a single rendered data table (no plot, micrograph or spectrum), captioned "Key microstructural parameters measured by EBSD and HRTEM for low density steels after solution-treatment". Its six columns are: Steel; D_FCC-G/T (μm); f_Tw/%; f_Bcc/%; D_Bcc/um (printed with "um", not "μm"); and D_κ-carbides/nm. Twelve conditions are arranged in three block rows: Fe30Mn 11Al (x)C — C-0.6, C-1.0, C-1.2, C-1.5; Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C — Mn-20, Mn-25, Mn-30, Mn-35; and Fe30Mn (x)Al 1C — Al-6, Al-8, Al-10, Al-11, Al-12. Every entry is a mean ± standard deviation. Ferrite is listed only for four conditions: C-0.6 (f_Bcc 30%, D_Bcc 5.5 ± 1.4 μm), Mn-20 (3.30%, 4.1 ± 0.7 μm), Mn-25 (0.65%, 4.5 ± 0.7 μm) and Al-12 (3.08%, 4.5 ± 0.9 μm); all other rows show a dash. With rising C, D_FCC-G/T grows from 7.3 ± 1.2 to about 22–24 μm, f_Tw falls from 56.7 to 50.2%, and D_κ-carbides coarsens from 1.0 ± 0.4 to 50 ± 18 nm. With rising Mn, D_FCC-G/T grows 9.9 → 33 μm while κ-carbides shrink 18 ± 6 → 2.0 ± 1.1 nm. With rising Al, D_FCC-G/T falls 34.2 → 12.6 μm and κ-carbides grow from 0ᵃ to 15 ± 6 nm. The table supplies the quantitative basis for the claim that κ-carbide size, not grain size, ferrite fraction or twin-boundary fraction, controls strength.

observations.observation: Table 3 has six column headers exactly as printed: Steel, D_FCC-G/T (μm), f_Tw/%, f_Bcc/%, D_Bcc/um, D_κ-carbides/nm; the ferrite grain-size column is printed with 'um' rather than the symbol μm.
Rows are grouped under three block labels: 'Fe30Mn 11Al (x)C', 'Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C' and 'Fe30Mn (x)Al 1C', covering twelve conditions (C-0.6 to C-1.5, Mn-20 to Mn-35, Al-6 to Al-12).
A ferrite volume fraction is listed for only four conditions: C-0.6 (30%), Mn-20 (3.30%), Mn-25 (0.65%) and Al-12 (3.08%); every other row carries a dash in both the f_Bcc and D_Bcc columns.
In the Fe30Mn11Al(x)C series, D_FCC-G/T increases from 7.3 ± 1.2 μm (C-0.6) to 23.7 ± 1.3 μm (C-1.0) and remains at about 22–24 μm for C-1.2 and C-1.5.
In the Fe30Mn11Al(x)C series, f_Tw decreases monotonically from 56.7% (C-0.6) through 53.9%, 51.8% to 50.2% (C-1.5).
The κ-carbide diameter in the C series increases monotonically: 1.0 ± 0.4 nm (C-0.6), 3.0 ± 0.6 nm (C-1.0), 20 ± 6 nm (C-1.2), 50 ± 18 nm (C-1.5).
In the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series, D_FCC-G/T increases from 9.9 ± 1.3 μm (Mn-20) to 33 ± 1.6 μm (Mn-35) while D_κ-carbides decreases from 18 ± 6 nm (Mn-20) to 2.0 ± 1.1 nm (Mn-35).

In the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C series, D_FCC-G/T decreases from 34.2 ± 1.1 μm (Al-6) to 12.6 ± 1.2 μm (Al-12), and κ-carbide size rises from the footnote-a value '0' (Al-6, Al-8) through 1.0 ± 0.4 nm (Al-10) and 3.0 ± 0.6 nm (Al-11) to 15 ± 6 nm (Al-12).
Rows Mn-30, Al-11 and C-1.0 carry identical values (23.7 ± 1.3 μm, 53.9%, dash, dash, 3.0 ± 0.6 nm), consistent with a shared Fe30Mn11Al1C reference composition.

Footnote 'a' states that the carbide diameter or the short-range ordering of Al and C is estimated to be very small from TEM investigations and it is assumed that no hardening is obtained from these features.

The caption states the tabulated parameters were measured by EBSD and HRTEM on low-density steels after solution-treatment; the image itself is only a table and cannot confirm the measurement techniques.

The citing text reports that for the Fe30Mn11Al0.6C steel both FCC austenite and BCC ferrite (about 30% by volume fraction) are present after solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching, with ferrite grain size about 5.5 μm and austenite grain size 7.3 μm.

The citing text states that the fractional twin boundary length f_Tw decreases from close to 60% in the 0.6%C sample to 50% in the 1.5%C sample, citing Table 3; the table itself prints 56.7% and 50.2% respectively, so the text value is a rounding of the table entry.

The citing text states that the average austenite grain size is larger in ferrite-free compositions, e.g. 22.5 μm in Fe30Mn11Al1.0C and 34.2 μm in Fe30Mn6Al1.0C, and that small amounts of ferrite should be designed in to refine the grain size.

The citing text uses Table 3 to argue that strength is mainly controlled by κ-carbide size rather than grain size, ferrite volume fraction or twin boundary fraction, noting that Fe1C30Mn6Al contains no κ-carbides while κ-carbides reach 50 nm in Fe1.5C30Mn11Al.

subfigures.description: Single rendered data table (Table 3) with six columns — Steel, D_FCC-G/T (μm), f_Tw/%, f_Bcc/%, D_Bcc/um, D_κ-carbides/nm — and twelve rows in three composition blocks: Fe30Mn 11Al (x)C (C-0.6, C-1.0, C-1.2, C-1.5), Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C (Mn-20, Mn-25, Mn-30, Mn-35), Fe30Mn (x)Al 1C (Al-6, Al-8, Al-10, Al-11, Al-12). All values are mean ± SD; dashes mark conditions for which ferrite fraction/grain size are not reported, and footnote 'a' marks the two carbide-free Al alloys.

unreadable_items: The meaning of the dash ('−') entries in the f_Bcc and D_Bcc columns is not defined in the caption (read here as 'phase absent / not measured').
The caption's fragmentary symbol definition 'D_FCC-G/T.' is incomplete, so the exact definition of the D_FCC-G/T column (grain vs. twin-related FCC size) is not stated in the caption itself.
Some cells are line-wrapped in the rendering (e.g. '5.5 ±\n1.4', '23.7 ±\n1.3'), which requires joining wrapped lines; the values themselves are legible.
